entities.summary: Mehmet Güney was a Turkish diplomat and international judge who played a crucial role in shaping the modern era of international law. Born in Siirt, Turkey in 1936, Güney served as a judge at the International Court of Justice from 1971 to 2002 and was a key figure in the development of the Convention on the Law of Treaties. His diplomatic career spanned over four decades, during which he served as a high-ranking official in the Turkish Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Güney was a vocal advocate for the rights of minority groups and was instrumental in shaping Turkey's foreign policy during the Cold War era. He died on April 24, 2024, leaving behind a legacy of promoting international cooperation and the rule of law. As he once said, 'The law is not a static concept, but a dynamic and evolving force that must adapt to the changing needs of humanity.'
